{"id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-9f2795b24322", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "An Application Load Balancer (ALB) works at Layer 7 and understands HTTP. A Network Load Balancer (NLB) works at Layer 4 and forwards TCP, UDP, and TLS traffic without looking inside it.

| | **ALB** | **NLB** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP |
| **Routing** | Content-based. Rules match on path, host header, HTTP headers, query strings, source IP, or HTTP method. | Connection-based. Routes by protocol and port, using a flow hash. |
| **Performance** | Good for web workloads. It adds some latency because it parses requests. | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency. It handles millions of requests per second and sudden traffic spikes. |
| **IP addressing** | Dynamic IPs. You use the DNS name. | One static IP per AZ, and you can attach Elastic IPs. It also supports PrivateLink. |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, and ALBs (so you can put an NLB in front of an ALB) |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS and supports SNI with multiple certificates. It can authenticate users with Cognito or OIDC. | Can terminate or pass through TLS. Passthrough preserves end-to-end encryption. |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023). Older NLBs have to be configured for it. |
| **Source IP** | Client IP arrives in the `X-Forwarded-For` header. | Preserves the client source IP for instance targets. |
| **Extras** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, WAF integration | Works as a PrivateLink endpoint service, and supports static IPs for allow-listing |

**When to choose which**
- **ALB**: HTTP/HTTPS apps, microservices, or containers that need path- or host-based routing. It also suits Lambda targets, WAF, and auth at the load balancer.
- **NLB**: Non-HTTP protocols (databases, MQTT, gaming, custom TCP/UDP), extreme performance or low latency, static IPs for firewall allow-lists, or exposing a service through PrivateLink.

You can also combine them. An NLB in front of an ALB gives you static IPs and PrivateLink support along with Layer 7 routing.

I can look at the load balancers in your account if you want. For example, I could check which ones you have and how they're configured.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
